Cross-Temporal Representational Similarity Analysis (CTRSA)¶

neurora.ctrdm_cal module¶

A module for calculating cross-temporal RDMs based on EEG-like data.

neurora.ctrdm_cal.ctRDM(data, chl_opt=0, time_win=5, time_step=5)¶

Calculate cross-temporal RDMs for EEG-like data.

Parameters:

  • data (array_like, shape [n_cons, n_subs, n_chls, n_ts]) –

    EEG-like data.

    n_cons, n_subs, n_chls, and n_ts represent the number of conditions, subjects, channels, and time points, respectively.

  • chl_opt (int, default=0) –

    Whether to calculate channel-specific CTRDMs.

    • 0 : calculate CTRDMs after combining channels and time points

    • 1 : calculate CTRDMs separately for each channel

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Time-window size for calculating CTRDMs.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows.

Returns:

ctrdms – Cross-temporal RDMs.

If chl_opt=0, the shape is:

[n_subs, n_windows, n_windows, n_cons, n_cons]

If chl_opt=1, the shape is:

[n_subs, n_chls, n_windows, n_windows, n_cons, n_cons]

Return type:

ndarray

Notes

This function always returns subject-level CTRDMs.

If you want the group-averaged CTRDMs, use:

np.nanmean(ctrdms, axis=0)

neurora.ctrdm_corr module¶

A module for calculating correlations between two cross-temporal RDMs.

neurora.ctrdm_corr.ctrdm_correlation_spearman(ctrdm1, ctrdm2)¶

Calculate the Spearman correlation between two CTRDMs.

Parameters:

  • ctrdm1 (array_like, shape [n_cons, n_cons]) – First cross-temporal RDM.

  • ctrdm2 (array_like, shape [n_cons, n_cons]) – Second cross-temporal RDM.

Returns:

corr – Spearman correlation result.

corr[0] is the correlation coefficient. corr[1] is the p-value.

Return type:

ndarray, shape [2]

Notes

Unlike standard symmetric RDMs, CTRDMs are not assumed to be symmetric. Therefore, all off-diagonal elements are used, not just the upper triangle.

neurora.ctcorr_cal module¶

A module for calculating cross-temporal similarities.

neurora.ctcorr_cal.ctsim_cal(data1, data2, chl_opt=0, time_win=5, time_step=5)¶

Calculate cross-temporal similarities between neural data under two conditions.

Parameters:

  • data1 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_chls, n_ts]) – EEG/MEG/fNIRS-like data under two conditions.

  • data2 (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_chls, n_ts]) – EEG/MEG/fNIRS-like data under two conditions.

  • chl_opt (int, default=0) –

    Whether to calculate channel-specific cross-temporal similarities.

    • 0 : combine channels and time points as features

    • 1 : calculate similarities separately for each channel

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Time-window size.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows.

Returns:

ctsimilarities – Cross-temporal similarities.

If chl_opt=0, shape is:

[n_subs, n_windows, n_windows, 2]

If chl_opt=1, shape is:

[n_subs, n_chls, n_windows, n_windows, 2]

The last dimension contains [r, p].

Return type:

ndarray

neurora.ctcorr_cal.ctsim_ctrdms_cal(ctrdms, model_rdm)¶

Calculate cross-temporal similarities between CTRDMs and a model RDM.

Parameters:

  • ctrdms (array_like, shape [n_ts, n_ts, n_cons, n_cons] or [..., n_ts, n_ts, n_cons, n_cons]) –

    Cross-temporal RDMs.

    The leading dimensions can represent subjects, channels, ROIs, etc.

  • model_rdm (array_like, shape [n_cons, n_cons]) – Model RDM.

Returns:

ctsimilarities – Cross-temporal similarities.

If ctrdms has shape [n_ts, n_ts, n_cons, n_cons], output shape is:

[n_ts, n_ts, 2]

If ctrdms has shape […, n_ts, n_ts, n_cons, n_cons], output shape is:

[…, n_ts, n_ts, 2]

The last dimension contains [r, p].

Return type:

ndarray

Notes

CTRDMs are not assumed to be symmetric. Therefore, all off-diagonal elements are used when correlating each CTRDM with the model RDM.

neurora.ctcorr_cal.ctsim_rdms_cal(rdms)¶

Calculate cross-temporal similarities based on temporal RDMs.

Parameters:

rdms (array_like, shape [n_ts, n_cons, n_cons] or [..., n_ts, n_cons, n_cons]) –

Temporal RDMs.

The leading dimensions can represent subjects, channels, ROIs, etc.

Returns:

ctsimilarities – Cross-temporal similarities.

If rdms has shape [n_ts, n_cons, n_cons], output shape is:

[n_ts, n_ts, 2]

If rdms has shape […, n_ts, n_cons, n_cons], output shape is:

[…, n_ts, n_ts, 2]

The last dimension contains [r, p].

Return type:

ndarray
